passage: On the third night, the seniors gathered the first-years in the hostel common room. “Belong first, belong properly,” one said. Each fresher was told to stand on a chair and announce that they were useless, then carry a senior's bag around the block. Most did it, laughing tightly. Nikita went along, eyes on the floor. Devika stepped forward when her turn came and said, “I'll introduce myself, but I won't do that.” The room went quiet. One senior sneered. Devika walked out with her heart pounding. That same evening she found the warden, Mrs Iyer, and told her everything. Mrs Iyer listened without interrupting, said, “You did the right thing, and none of this is your fault,” and phoned the head of the anti-ragging committee while Devika was still in the room. Next morning Nikita knocked on the warden's door too.

qa.q: What was each fresher told to announce while standing on a chair?
qa.a: Each fresher was told to announce that they were useless.

qa.q: What might Devika have been feeling as Devika walked out with her heart pounding?
qa.a: Devika was probably frightened and shaky, and also sure that she did not want to be humiliated, even though she wanted to belong.

qa.q: What did Mrs Iyer do that same evening after Devika told her?
qa.a: Mrs Iyer listened without interrupting, told Devika it was not her fault and phoned the head of the anti-ragging committee while Devika was still there.

qa.q: What might Nikita have been feeling while going along with the tasks with eyes on the floor?
qa.a: Nikita was probably uncomfortable and afraid of being left out, going along to belong, which may be why Nikita knocked on the warden's door the next morning.

grounding: A new student is asked to do humiliating tasks to join a group, and one who refuses reports it the same day and an adult acts.

passage:
Dear Pooja,
You asked why I sounded odd on the phone. Here it is. The rowing club's welcome week was supposed to be fun. On the first night the seniors made us stand in the hall and shout that we were nobodies. On the second we carried their bags and sang in the dining hall while they filmed. On the third they wanted us to do a dare I knew was unsafe. I wanted so badly to belong that I nearly did. Instead I said no and walked out. On Friday I went to the faculty adviser. She listened, said it wasn't my fault, and called both captains in that same afternoon. I'm still shaky, and a few first-years won't talk to me. But two of them came to my room yesterday.
Asif

qa.q: What did the seniors make the newcomers do on the first night?
qa.a: The seniors made them stand in the hall and shout that they were nobodies.

qa.q: Why did Asif say, “I wanted so badly to belong that I nearly did”?
qa.a: Asif felt a strong pull to belong and almost gave in to a dare, even though Asif knew it was unsafe.

qa.q: What did the faculty adviser do that same afternoon?
qa.a: The faculty adviser listened, told Asif it was not Asif's fault and called both captains in that afternoon.

qa.q: What might the two first-years who came to Asif's room yesterday have been feeling?
qa.a: They may have felt relieved and a little ashamed, and may have wanted Asif's company after seeing Asif refuse.

grounding: A new student is asked to do humiliating and unsafe tasks to join a group, refuses and reports it to an adult who acts the same day.

passage: Avni, before you go to the hostel, let your Anirban mama tell you something. In my first week of engineering college, the seniors called us freshers up to the terrace at midnight. They said joining the 'family' meant doing whatever they asked. First it was singing, which was silly but fine. Then they told my roommate Pradeep to take off his shirt and stand in the cold. I wanted so badly to belong that I almost laughed along. Pradeep was shaking. Something in me said no. I walked him down the stairs, and the next morning we went together to the warden and the anti-ragging committee. The seniors were suspended. For a month some people wouldn't talk to us. Then others started saying thank you. Belonging that needs someone humiliated isn't belonging.

qa.q: Where did the seniors call the freshers at midnight?
qa.a: Up to the terrace.

qa.q: Why did young Anirban almost laugh along?
qa.a: He wanted so badly to belong that going along felt safer than standing out, even while he was uneasy.

qa.q: Which choice in the story was the turning point, and why did it matter?
qa.a: Walking Pradeep down and reporting to the warden and anti-ragging committee the next morning; it stopped the harm and protected others.

qa.q: What was it like for Pradeep on the terrace?
qa.a: Pradeep was shaking and humiliated, likely frightened and powerless in front of the seniors.

grounding: An uncle recalls how the wish to belong nearly led him to accept a humiliating initiation, until he protected his roommate and reported it.

passage: Sarika had been in Pune for nine days, knew nobody, and her phone was broken, so she couldn't even call home. The college dance society was the first place that felt friendly. Then the seniors said new members had to 'earn their place': wash the seniors' practice clothes, stay silent at meals, and never tell the teachers. Two other first-years did it without complaint. Sarika scrubbed a pile of T-shirts in the hostel bathroom till midnight, telling herself this was belonging. The next day her classmate Uday saw her raw hands. 'That's ragging,' he said quietly. 'You don't have to earn a club.' That afternoon they went together to the society's faculty adviser, who called the seniors in the same day, ended the 'tasks' and told Sarika she was welcome at practice.

qa.q: How long had Sarika been in Pune?
qa.a: Nine days.

qa.q: Why did Sarika keep scrubbing till midnight?
qa.a: She was lonely and desperate to belong, with no phone to call home, so she told herself the tasks were part of joining.

qa.q: What made Uday's response helpful?
qa.a: He named it as ragging, said she didn't have to earn a club, and went with her to the faculty adviser the same day.

qa.q: How might the two first-years who did the tasks without complaint be feeling?
qa.a: They may also feel humiliated but afraid of losing their place, and relieved when the adviser ended the tasks.

grounding: A lonely new student accepts humiliating tasks to belong until a classmate names it and an adult ends it the same day.

passage: In his second week at a Delhi college, Hrithik was told by the cricket team's seniors that every fresher had to ride the metro wearing a cardboard sign saying 'I AM A DONKEY' and bray at each station. The other freshers laughed nervously. Hrithik's stomach dropped, but he wanted the team so badly that he picked up the marker. Mohit, a second-year player, walked in. 'No. We're not doing this anymore.' A senior argued, 'It's tradition, it builds bonding.' Mohit said, 'Then let's bond at a five a.m. run at the stadium. All of us, seniors too.' Grumbling, they agreed. The next morning, twelve players ran laps in the dark, freshers and seniors panting together. Hrithik still told the sports teacher about the sign, and a no-ragging rule went up on the notice board.

qa.q: What did the sign say?
qa.a: 'I AM A DONKEY'.

qa.q: What was Hrithik feeling when he picked up the marker?
qa.a: His stomach dropped; he felt humiliated and anxious, but wanted to join the team so badly that he nearly went along.

qa.q: How did Mohit keep the bonding but remove the harm?
qa.a: Mohit refused the humiliating task and replaced it with a five a.m. run for everyone, seniors too, so the shared effort had no victim.

qa.q: How might the senior who called it tradition feel?
qa.a: Probably annoyed and defensive at first, but running laps with the freshers may show that bonding doesn't need humiliation.

grounding: A new student is pushed toward a humiliating initiation; a senior replaces it with shared hardship without harm, and a teacher is told.

passage:
"Fresher! Up on the chair. Sing the song, and after every line say 'I am nothing'." Akash grinned. Six seniors crowded the corridor, phones out.
"Why?" Tenzin asked.
"Because that's how you become one of us. We all did it."
"Everyone does it, bro," muttered Karan, the other fresher, already climbing onto a chair.
Tenzin's face burned. He wanted the Saturday football, the jokes at mess, a nickname of his own. "I'll play on your team. I'll carry the kit. I'm not doing this."
"Then enjoy eating alone for four years."
That night Tenzin knocked on the warden's door. "Sir, they're making freshers do things on video. Karan too."
Mr Lobo put down his pen. "Thank you for telling me. You've done nothing wrong. I'm coming to the corridor now, and those videos will be deleted tonight."

qa.q: How many seniors crowded the corridor?
qa.a: Six seniors crowded the corridor, phones out.

qa.q: How did Tenzin feel when Akash ordered him onto the chair?
qa.a: He wanted badly to belong, the football, the jokes, a nickname, but felt humiliated by the task, so the wish and the refusal pulled against each other.

qa.q: What did Tenzin do that protected himself and others?
qa.a: He offered fair ways to belong, refused the humiliating task, and told the warden that same night, mentioning that Karan was involved too.

qa.q: How might Karan be feeling as he climbs onto the chair?
qa.a: Karan may feel scared and resigned, going along because refusing seems to cost more than the humiliation.

grounding: Shows a new student pressed to do humiliating tasks to belong, refusing, and a warden acting the same night.
